title: Nvidia, Broadcom shielded as AI power crunch hits chip supply chain, says Morgan Stanley
source_used: Reuters text (by Kanishka Ajmera) on The Lufkin Daily News and The Economic Times copies. Reuters original not opened (HTTP 401).
key_facts: Morgan Stanley said on Monday 5 Oct 2026 that Nvidia and Broadcom are relatively insulated from a worsening US data-center power crunch.
Any resulting delay in AI deployments can affect makers of memory, optical and other secondary chip components.
The brokerage estimated last month that US data-center developers face a 34% net power shortfall through 2028, equal to 32 GW, after measures such as behind-the-meter generation and fuel cells.

Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs have both flagged mounting constraints on the US data-center buildout; GS expects limited near-term impact from political pushback, while MS sees labor, power and political challenges.

Morgan Stanley does not see the bottlenecks putting Nvidia's or Broadcom's 2027 forecasts at risk, citing their visibility into chip placement, geographic expansion and coordination with data centers and power supply.
If chip capacity cannot be deployed, customers could push out deliveries or cancel orders; memory, optics, power-management and analog components are most exposed to inventory disruption.
quote_evidence: Oct 5 (Reuters) - Nvidia and Broadcom are relatively insulated from a worsening US data-center power crunch, but any resultant delay in AI deployments can affect makers of memory, optical and other secondary chip components, Morgan Stanley said on Monday.

If chip capacity cannot be deployed, customers could push out deliveries or cancel orders, with memory, optics, power-management and analog components most exposed to inventory disruption, the brokerage said.

The brokerage estimated last month that US data-center developers face a 34% net power shortfall through 2028, equivalent to 32 GW, after accounting for measures such as behind-the-meter generation and fuel cells
why_it_matters_hint: Power limits for US AI data centres could delay chip use, hitting parts makers more than Nvidia or Broadcom, according to one brokerage.
